verses.commentary: The prophet takes his stand at the watchtower, stations himself on the ramparts. He will watch to see what God says. The posture of expectant waiting. Faith waits for divine response. Complaint requires receptivity to answer.

The Lord replies. Write the revelation, make it plain on tablets so a herald can run with it. The message must be clear, portable, transmissible. Clarity enables proclamation. What God reveals must be shared.

The revelation awaits appointed time. It speaks of the end and will not prove false. Though it lingers, wait for it. It will certainly come without delay. Prophetic patience. Timing belongs to God. Certainty does not mean immediacy.

The enemy is puffed up, desires not upright. But the righteous will live by his faithfulness (or faith). The pivotal verse. Paul quotes this in Romans 1:17 and Galatians 3:11. The righteous survive through trust in God, not through power or achievement.

Wine betrays the arrogant. Never at rest. Greedy as the grave, like death never satisfied. Gathering nations, taking peoples captive. The contrast: the righteous live by faith; the arrogant are driven by insatiable greed. Two ways of being in the world.
First woe begins. Will not all taunt the oppressor? Woe to him who piles up stolen goods, makes himself rich by extortion. How long? The plundered will find voice. Victims will mock victimizers.
Will not creditors suddenly arise? Make you tremble? You become their prey. Those you oppressed become your oppressors. Debts come due. Role reversal. The economic imagery: debtor becomes creditor.

Because you plundered many nations, the remnant will plunder you. Human blood shed, lands and cities destroyed. Violence rebounds. What goes around comes around. The law of consequence operates across history.
Second woe. Building house by unjust gain, setting nest on high to escape ruin. The image of a bird building secure nest above danger. But height provides no safety from divine judgment.
You plotted ruin for many peoples, shamed your own house, forfeited your life. Self destruction through destroying others. The house built on injustice collapses on its builder.

Stones cry out from the wall, beams of woodwork echo it. Even construction materials testify against unjust builders. Creation witnesses against exploitation. The very fabric of ill gotten wealth accuses.
Third woe. Building city with bloodshed, establishing town by injustice. Urban development through violence. Cities built on corpses. Civilization's foundations examined and found wanting.
Has not the Lord determined that peoples' labor is fuel for fire? Nations exhaust themselves for nothing. When God judges, human achievement burns. All the striving produces only ash.

The earth will be filled with knowledge of the Lord's glory as waters cover the sea. The vision beyond judgment. Ultimate purpose: not destruction but revelation. Divine glory manifest throughout creation.
Fourth woe. Giving drink to neighbors, making them drunk to gaze on their nakedness. Using intoxication to exploit vulnerability. Creating helplessness for personal advantage. Power abused sexually.
Filled with shame instead of glory. Your turn to drink! Nakedness exposed! The cup from the Lord's right hand comes around. Disgrace covers glory. What you did to others is done to you.

Violence done to Lebanon (deforestation), destruction of animals (environmental devastation), human blood shed, lands and cities destroyed. Ecological violence joins human violence. Creation care is a prophetic concern.

Of what value is an idol carved by a craftsman? An image that teaches lies? The maker trusts his own creation. Makes mute idols. The absurdity: creating your god, then worshipping it. Self made religion is self deception.

Fifth woe. Saying to wood 'come alive!' to stone 'wake up!' Can it give guidance? Covered in gold and silver but no breath. Idols are dead despite decoration. No life, no wisdom, no help. The decorations mock the emptiness.

The Lord is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him. Contrast with idols: the living God is present. Appropriate response: silence. Not empty silence but reverent attention. The noisy self assertion of wickedness yields to sacred stillness.
